I don't have any notes on Psalm 5 for you yet, because my research tool was blocked before I could open a single source. When I tried to fetch the pages, the tool told me I had no calls left for this turn, and it gave me no content. My other tools have no internet access, so I couldn't work around it.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any notes from memory.

I got as far as picking these pages to read first:

- **Verse-by-verse:** Enduring Word on Psalm 5, Precept Austin's Psalm 5 commentary, and the Bible Hub commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit).
- **Tradition-specific:** Calvin's commentary on CCEL (Reformed), Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (Baptist) and Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu (Methodist). For Lutheran, Pentecostal and Anglican views I'd search the sites you listed.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, Augustine's exposition of Psalm 5 on New Advent (Catholic), and any OCA material. I'd also check for discussion of prosperity or word-of-faith readings of v. 12 ("You bless the righteous…").

If you ask again in a new message, my tool access should reset and I'll do the research and write the notes in the "v. 4: …" format, with a URL for every point.
